$comment: The hero's text safe zones. DECISIONS.md D-22 puts DOM type over the room,
and type over a rendered scene needs a contrast guarantee that a token pair
cannot give: --ground means nothing when the pixels behind the words are
floor catching spill. So the guarantee is made against rendered pixels, and
WHY THE RECTANGLES ARE WIDER THAN THE TEXT. The gate applies one set of
fractions at both 1440x900 and 390x844, so each rectangle here is the UNION
of the measured text box at those two viewports. At 1440 the headline is
1030x206 at 40,172; at 390 it is 350x158 at 20,137. Neither fraction set
covers the other, so the union is what actually contains the words at both,
and it is a stricter constraint than either one alone. Measured in built
output, not computed from the stylesheet.
WHEN A ZONE FAILS, MOVE THE LIGHT. In order: raise the optical axis, dim
--hero-fill (0.22, may go to 0.16), narrow HERO_Y.fanExtent, move the
headline further into the upper left. Adding a panel or a scrim behind the
type is not on the list and never becomes one.

exempt.why: The install strip carries its own opaque surface and is the one element that is meant to be the brightest thing in the frame.
